    Breaking: What Should You Do With Pumpkins After Halloween?

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (995 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Familyhandyman

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Should you compost pumpkins after Halloween, toss them in the trash or leave them out for wildlife?
    • In a recent development, before they migrated to North America, the Irish and Scottish immigrants who established the tradition of jack-o’-lanterns, carved turnips.
    • “One billion (with a B!),” exclaims composter Lauren Click, and that’s not good, because not everyone responsibly disposes of their jack-o’-lanterns responsibly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

    Should you compost pumpkins after Halloween, toss them in the trash or leave them out for wildlife? Experts explain the options.

    In a recent development, before they migrated to North America, the Irish and Scottish immigrants who established the tradition of jack-o’-lanterns, carved turnips. In the New World, they started carving pumpkins, which were readily available and far more dramatic. Since then, the Halloween tradition they established in the 19th century has only grown more popular and sees more and more pumpkins discarded every year.

    How many? “One billion (with a B!),” exclaims composter Lauren Click, and that’s not good, because not everyone responsibly disposes of their jack-o’-lanterns responsibly.

    If you care about soil, wildlife and the environment in general, there really is a right way and a wrong way to dispose of pumpkins after Halloween. A gardening expert, a composting expert and a worm farmer explain the difference.

    It has been revealed that definitely, yes. “There are many ways to compost a pumpkin,” claims Click. “I chop mine up into smaller pieces and feed it to my indoor worm compost farm. You can compost all parts of a pumpkin as long as it is not treated with chemicals, has no paint (so, no painted pumpkins), no glitter, and no plastic/wax/metal candle residue. You can even compost moldy/gross pumpkins!”.

    It’s important to chop up the pumpkin and not throw it on the compost pile whole, adds UK gardener David Denyer. “Pumpkins decompose slowly if left whole because of their thick rind and high water content. Because of this, adding them straight to your compost can throw off the balance, making the heap turn slimy or even anaerobic, which stops it from breaking down properly.”.

    One option is to give them to animal rescues and local farmers to use as feed for pigs, chickens and livestock. Click loves this option because, as she says, many farmers compost manure, which makes it a win-win situation. The pumpkin winds up providing nourishment in the soil for more pumpkins.

    If you live in the city, worm farmer Scott Kent has another suggestion: “Take your leftover pumpkins is to a worm farm! Composting worms, like red wigglers, consume organic waste and create worm castings from it. Pumpkins, and most all other cucurbits for that matter, are among composting worms’ most favorite foods.”.

    In a recent development, for a quick way to recycle pumpkins after Halloween that you can do at home, cut the pumpkin into small chunks and bury them in your garden. “This works like a green manure,” says Denyer, “adding organic matter below the surface where it can decompose safely without attracting any pests or spreading disease.”.

    This is generally a bad idea, say our experts. Click worries about attracting wildlife to areas in which they can be harmed, but beyond that, decomposing pumpkins are not the best source of nutrition. “The acidity and mold that develops as they rot can make hedgehogs, insects, and birds unwell,” says Denyer, who lives where hedgehogs are a thing.

    Sources indicate that the danger to wildlife increases if the pumpkin contains toxic materials. If you wouldn’t feed, paint, glitter or candle wax to a pet, you shouldn’t feed it to wildlife.

    Before carving a pumpkin, most people remove the seeds. Don’t throw them out. When you roast them, they make a delicious snack. After the seeds are gone, the rind makes a good (if temporary) planter for displaying your fall blooms on the porch. Just remember to line the inside to prevent dirt from spilling out from the face you carved.

    Industry observers note that composting may be the best way to recycle a pumpkin rind, but if you’re okay with a less dramatic jack-o’-lantern, a smaller pumpkin like a Hokkaido or Baby-Bear can serve a double purpose. Unlike large carving pumpkins with thick, waxy skins, these smaller varieties have thin skins and a high sugar content that make them delicious in soup.

    Industry observers note that don’t just toss  them in the garden, warns Denyer: “Pumpkins are high in water and sugars, which means they quickly break down into a thick, slimy layer that blocks air circulation and traps moisture around plant roots. This can then encourage fungal problems, like grey mold or powdery mildew, which can spread to nearby plants.”.

    In a recent development, it’s notable to check with the local waste management rules, because some communities don’t allow pumpkins in yard waste bins. If your community allows them, remove candle wax and other inorganic materials.

    Painted pumpkins present a problem: They are organic, but because of the paint, you shouldn’t throw them in organic waste, and some communities prohibit organic materials in the general trash. In such cases, cutting up and burying your pumpkins after Halloween is probably the best solution.

    Industry observers note that if you leave a whole pumpkin out in the field, it will start decomposing about eight or 12 weeks after it’s fully ripe. Once you cut a pumpkin into smaller pieces and throw them in a compost pile, the pieces will start to rot in five to 10 days.

    Full decomposition depends on the moisture content of the air and soil, and on the temperature. It occurs faster when there’s lots of moisture and the air is warm.

    According to recent reports, generally, no. Most paints contain toxic chemicals that can poison the compost and the soil on which you spread it. This isn’t necessarily true for all paints, including some water-soluble plant- or egg-based children’s paints, but if you don’t know where the paint came from, keep the painted pumpkin out of the compost.

    It has been revealed that A paint may be safe for kids, but that doesn’t mean it’s safe for composting. Crayola, a manufacturer of safe-to-use paints for children, recommends using them on pumpkins but warns that those pumpkins should not be consumed (meaning they should not go in the compost).

    The chief investigator for the Dallas County public defender’s office was arrested and charged with first-degree murder Saturday after his wife was found dead in their apartment.

    Jimmy Harold Spurger Jr., 54, who has worked for the public defender’s office for nearly 14 years, was married to his wife, Maria Teresa Spurger, for 35 years but filed for divorce in late October, according to Fox 4.

    Local first responders who were conducting a welfare check Friday night forced their way into the apartment, where they found Spurger’s wife unresponsive on a couch with a knife in her neck, Fox 4 reports. Spurger also was found in the apartment, covered in blood and sitting next to a knife in the bedroom.

    After responding officers found multiple pill bottles also covered in blood, they suspected that Spurger had ingested pills and transported him to the hospital, Fox 4 reports. He was later taken into custody and is being held on a $1 million bond.

    Spurger has led the Investigative Division for the Dallas County public defender’s office for 11 months, Fox 4 reports. Previously, he spent more than 13 years in its Capital Murder Division. He also worked for more than 20 years in law enforcement, which included supervising investigations in the Child Abuse and Family Violence Division of the Dallas County district attorney’s office.

    Dallas County Chief Public Defender Christi Dean told Fox 4 that Spurger was “an exemplary colleague,” and that “it’s hard to imagine that he has been charged with murder.”.

    In a recent development, “We know in our profession that the probable cause affidavit doesn’t tell the whole story,” Dean also reportedly remarked. “The media reports don’t tell the whole story. And we’re still in preliminary stages.”.

    Breaking: Yard Eyesores That Ruin Your Curb Appeal

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Realtors weigh in on these common yard eyesores that can hurt curb appeal and make a home look less than its best.
    • Industry observers note that what makes a yard an eyesore?
    • Industry observers note that the good news is that nobody has to agree on what makes one yard beautiful and another an eyesore (unless you live in an HOA!), but some yard features are bound to cause a head shake or two from the neighbors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

    Realtors weigh in on these common yard eyesores that can hurt curb appeal and make a home look less than its best.

    Industry observers note that what makes a yard an eyesore? It depends on who you ask. Like personal style and hygiene, everyone has different rules when it comes to yard upkeep and design. One person’s cherished garden gnomes might be another’s idea of tacky kitsch. Lawn decor might be a matter of taste, but neglected maintenance like a broken fence or rotting RV in the yard are harder to overlook.

    Industry observers note that the good news is that nobody has to agree on what makes one yard beautiful and another an eyesore (unless you live in an HOA!), but some yard features are bound to cause a head shake or two from the neighbors. Ahead, find some of the most controversial yard eyesores, with a reminder that curb appeal is always subjective.

    Sources indicate that unmowed grass and overgrown weeds make a yard look neglected and can rapidly crossover into eyesore territory. But that doesn’t mean everyone’s yard has to look perfectly manicured or exactly the same, either. “A yard that is basic is not a problem as long as it is well kept,” real estate broker Erik Leland states. “You could choose a meadow-style yard or a pollinator garden as long as it is intentional with defined paths and maintained edges.”.

    In a recent development, vibrant, healthy trees and shrubs add to a home’s curb appeal, but neglected, overgrown or dead ones can promptly tank it. Even if the rest of the yard is well-maintained, lifeless hedges and trees make it look like an eyesore. “Dead shrubs may appear minor. However, they create a larger perception glitch if the property owner is not maintaining something minor, like dead shrubs,” real estate agent Ben Mizes states.

    Sources indicate that broken or unused bulky items like patio furniture, piles of lumber, old furniture or broken lawn equipment can rapidly pile up in the yard and become an eyesore. Difficult to dispose of, these items can overwhelm homeowners. “When you see clutter and junk in or around a home, it can create stress and uneasiness, even for neighbors,” Realtor Dell Jeanty says. “Keeping the yard organized can make the property and the entire street feel cleaner and more welcoming.”.

    Fences can add to a home’s curb appeal and value, but a neglected one is just a yard eyesore. Broken, rotting and leaning fences drag down a property’s appeal and give the impression it’s not cared for. However, “a fence does not have to be new to look good,” real estate expert Cameron Walker notes. “Old fences can be painted, and neglected and damaged fences can be repaired to make a good first impression.”.

    Adding statues and garden gnomes to your yard is a personal choice that not everyone will enjoy. What makes you smile may make your neighbor scratch their head. But, even if you are a fan, it is possible to have too much of a good thing. “The right amount of decorations can give personality to a yard and make it inviting, but too many can give a cluttered appearance,” Walker claims. “Decorations should be placed to give ample space to display the landscaping.”.

    While low-maintenance artificial turf is appealing, it can look like an eyesore if not done correctly. Low-quality material and shoddy installation methods result in uneven seams and a cheap aesthetic. “One of the major problems is if it appears as if the grass has been glued to the ground,” Mizes indicates. But, even when done right, some people just don’t like the look of fake turf. It comes down to personal preference.

    It has been revealed that A few carefully placed ornaments can give a yard character, but too many create an eyesore of visual clutter. “A property can lose appeal with an overabundance of various garden ornaments competing for focal points throughout the landscape,” Mizes states. “[But] a collection within a defined area of the landscape can be better appreciated.” Just know that your vision of a beautiful yard might look like a flea market to your neighbor.

    Industry observers note that “There’s nothing wrong with having garbage and recycling bins in the front yard during pick-up day, but leaving them lined up in front of the house all week doesn’t look great and robs the home of its curb appeal,” Jeanty claims. “Tucking them beside the house or behind a small screen keeps the yard looking cleaner.” On the other hand, some folks just don’t see what the big deal is about hiding trash cans and that’s okay, too.

    According to recent reports, broken down cars, ATVs or campers strewn in a yard qualify as a yard eyesore in most people’s eyes. Mice settle in, lawn and weeds grow around it and your property can start to resemble a junk yard. It knocks down your curb appeal and impacts your home’s value and your neighbor’s, too. A non-working vehicle doesn’t automatically constitute an eyesore, though, if it’s stored intentionally and preferably out of sight.

    According to recent reports, while they may spread holiday cheer, not everyone cares for inflatable yard decorations. Where some see whimsy, others see tacky. No matter which side you’re on, most would agree that when deflated during the day, inflatables turn into a yard eyesore. “They just look like piles of plastic in your yard,” Leland says. Additionally, too many inflatables can be fun or make a yard look disorganized and cluttered, depending on your take.

    “A derelict shed or rotting play structure is sure to give a bad impression,” Leland says. “If it’s not worth repairing, remove it. An empty space is the better choice.” When I moved into my current home, one of the first things we did was remove a large gazebo that was long past its prime. Our newly introduced neighbors all came by and thanked us for removing the neighborhood eyesore.

    Kitschy lawn ornaments like plastic flamingos could elicit an eye roll from a neighbor, but perhaps not. “A couple of plastic flamingos can be funny and add personality to a yard, so I wouldn’t automatically call them an eyesore,” Jeanty says. “But when there are twenty of them with mismatched colors competing with signs, flags and other decorations, it becomes a little overwhelming.” Thoughtfully incorporate your outdoor decor into the landscape for a more tasteful display.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Abraham Teklu Lemma, 53, of Maryland, a former information technology contractor at the National Reconnaissance Office, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Department of Justice pleaded guilty today to conspiring to commit espionage on behalf of the government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia.

    Lemma pleaded guilty to conspiracy to transmit national defense information to a foreign government and has agreed to be incarcerated for a period of between 120 and 262 months.

    “Lemma betrayed the United States to an extraordinary degree,” mentioned Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “He exploited his IT administrator access to remove classified national defense information, including Top Secret information, from a secure facility and transmitted it to Ethiopian government officials hoping they would use it to target and kill paramilitary fighters in a regional conflict. Clearance holders pledge undivided loyalty to the United States and bear a legal and moral responsibility to protect classified information. Those who betray this trust will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.”.

    It has been revealed that “For more than two years, Lemma exploited a position of trust to provide highly classified U.S. government information to a foreign government,” stated U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia. “In doing so, he betrayed his oath, his colleagues, and his country, while jeopardizing our national security. His guilty plea sends a clear message: those who compromise America’s most sensitive secrets will be investigated, prosecuted, and held accountable.”.

    Industry observers note that “Despite swearing an oath to defend the Constitution of the United States, Abraham Lemma betrayed our country by committing espionage on behalf of the Ethiopian government,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “By his own admission, Lemma provided classified national defense information to Ethiopian officials, who then used it in military operations during an ongoing conflict. This guilty plea should serve notice that the FBI and our partners will work tirelessly to stop foreign intelligence services, and anyone who decides to work with them, against the interests of the United States.”.

    According to recent reports, “Today’s guilty plea makes clear that any attempt to betray the United States, violate the trust of the American people, and compromise our national security will not be tolerated,” stated Assistant Director in Charge Darren B. Cox of the FBI Washington Field Office. “Lemma abused his position of trust and access to some of our nation’s most highly classified information, conspiring with foreign government officials to unlawfully disclose materials protected to the highest level. In doing so, he not only endangered our national security but also betrayed the trust placed in him by the American people.”.

    In a recent development, according to court documents, Lemma held a Top Secret U.S. security clearance. From 2021 until his arrest in August 2023, Lemma conspired with senior Ethiopian government officials to collect and transmit dozens of highly classified documents, notes, materials, and photographs, classified up to the Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) level, to Ethiopian government officials. Material identified as “Top Secret” means that unauthorized disclosure of the material is reasonably to cause “exceptionally grave damage to the national security” of the United States.

    Much of the highly classified information Lemma shared with the Ethiopian government concerned an armed conflict in Ethiopia. Lemma’s conspirators included senior officials within political, military, and intelligence branches of the Ethiopian government.

    During his espionage activities, Lemma took numerous steps to conceal his conduct. and surreptitiously removed classified documents and information from U.S. government holdings.

    Sources indicate that specifically, Lemma wrote notes by hand with classified information and then hand-carried those notes out of secure U.S. government facilities. Additionally, as an IT administrator, Lemma removed electronic versions of classified information from classified U.S. government repositories and then removed the same classified information from secure U.S. government facilities where he worked.

    In a recent development, on some occasions, Lemma encouraged his Ethiopian government conspirators to take direct action against paramilitary groups who were fighting the government of Ethiopia. For example, on Dec. 18, 2021, Lemma told one conspirator, “We have to finish these people once and for all, otherwise there will never be peace in Ethiopia.” Later that day, Lemma shared additional information with his conspirator and wrote, “Please send Dro[nes].”.

    According to recent reports, according to the plea agreement, Lemma agreed to plead guilty to conspiracy to transmit national defense information to a foreign government. If accepted by the court, Lemma has agreed to be incarcerated for a period of between 120 and 262 months. Sentencing is set for April 14, 2027.

    The FBI Washington Field Office investigated the case, with assistance from the U.S. Department of State's Diplomatic Security Service.

    The matter is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Tejpal Chawla and Adam P. Barry for the District of Columbia, and Trial Attorney Kathryn DeMarco of the Department of Justice’s National Security Division.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

    Your riding lawnmower can do double duty this winter by adding a snow plow. Here’s what you need to know before adding a plow to your riding mower.

    Sources indicate that snow is considered a “four-letter” word in our home. Living in the northeast, right in the middle of the so called “I-95” corridor, we usually average 20 inches of snow a year. Even with my trusted 26-inch two-stage snow blower and my newest gadget, an 18 volt snow shovel, clearing the driveway and sidewalk can quickly turn into a significant time consuming and dangerous job. If you already own a riding mower (different from a lawn or garden tractor), you may wonder if you can add a snow plow to turn it into a useful piece of year-round equipment.

    The short answer is “yes, maybe,” mentioned David Bodzioch, certified Small Engine and Automotive Technology Instructor. Snow (plow) blades are available for certain riding mowers. However, Bodzioch cautioned, “attaching a blade doesn’t necessarily make your mower ready to clean a snow-covered driveway.”.

    Accessory compatibility, traction, mower size as well as the amount and type of snow you typically need to move will determine if you can, or should, add a plow blade to your riding lawnmower. Before investing in a plow, you need to understand what your mower can realistically handle. As well as determining what accessories you might need. Here’s what our experts have to say about turning a riding mower into a snow plow.

    Recent findings suggest that “Yes, many riding lawnmowers can be equipped with a front-mounted snow blade,” remarked certified Small Engine instructor Jeffrey Cesari. “Even if aftermarket compatible attachments are available, you should use the manufacturer’s approved attachments,” added Cesari. “Adding a plow blade on small tractors requires a set of rear wheel chains and a counterweight for balance,” added Cesari.

    Sources indicate that for example, John Deere sells a front blade package (as well as snow throwers) designed for specific riding lawnmowers. A John Deer 19 horsepower or better twin-cylinder engine units position the driver closer to the engine for better balance.

    What Do You Need to Turn a Riding Lawnmower Into a Snow Plow?

    “At minimum, you’ll need a snow blade and direct-fit mounting hardware designed to fit your particular make and model mower,” mentioned Bodzioch. Tire chains and weights should also be considered when operating snow-clearing equipment. According to Troy-Bilt, makers of outdoor power equipment, “Depending on the riding lawnmower mower and snow conditions, the mower will benefit from the added traction that chains and weights provide” when removing snow.

    “It depends on whether your mower simply requires a blade, or the added cost of mounting hardware, weights and tire chains,” mentioned Cesari. An add on blade can cost as little as $120 for 22 to 32 inch width universal riding mower plow kit, to over $1400 for a complete John Deere 46 inch front blade snow plow package that includes an adjustable three-position blade height and angle setting you can change from the driver’s seat. Look for heavy-gauge steel blades that are height-adjustable and have the ability to reposition the shave plate for longer life.

    The biggest advantage is getting year-round use from expensive equipment you already own. Plus, eliminating the need for another piece of snow-removal equipment that sits unused for nine or ten months out of the year.

    “You’ll probably need to buy and install several accessories and that can be expensive,” stated Bodzioch. You should also check how difficult it is swapping out the snow blade and grass cutting mower deck. He added that “you also want check if your mower and blade combination are right for your type [concrete, blacktop, etc.] driveway.”.

    Yes, it can be, and should be, as long as your mower is approved for the attachment, is well-maintained and in good working condition. Following the manufacturer’s operating, maintenance guides and safety instructions is mandatory for safe and efficient operation; the same as when using any other piece of outdoor power equipment.

    In a recent development, bodzioch remarked, “Proper traction is especially important when driving on ice and snow, or on snow-covered grass or soil.” But Cesari also notes that “you need to be aware of frame structure and that adding a snow plow can cause frame damage, transmission wear and belt fatigue on small home riding mowers.” Cesari said plowing up to five inches should be safe. Always be cautious and use common sense if your mower is struggling while removing any amount of snow.

    It has been revealed that it depends. It may only make sense if you already own a compatible mower. However, having room and space to safely store the blade should be a real consideration. Cesari added, “Converting your mower to a plow may require buying expensive attachments or accessories. Consider a standalone snow blower or a lawn/garden tractor if it’s difficult swap out the mower deck and plow.” If you regularly deal with challenging snow conditions, a dedicated snow-removal machine may be the better investment.

    In a recent development, it depends on how you use the word. While “riding mower” and “lawn tractor” are often interchangeable, there are key differences between the two pieces of equipment. A riding mower typically means any mower you sit on, including a lawn tractor or zero-turn mower. Nevertheless, a lawn/garden tractor will generally be more expensive and have a larger, sturdier frame. Lawn/garden tractors are designed and built to accept manufacturers’ compatible direct-fit attachments and accessories.

    Sources indicate that jeffrey Cesari has been teaching Small Engine Technology at Bucks County Technical High School, located in Fairless Hills, PA. for over 30 years. Before teaching, Jeff operated his owned small engine repair shop. Jeff holds a Pennsylvania Department of Education teacher certificate in Small Engine Technology. He also won the prestigious Harbor Freight Tools for Schools Award, obtained a masters equivalence in industrial education. Jef is also a certified PennDoT safety inspector and instructor. Jeff also earned five industry recognized certifications, including 4-cycle and 2-cycle engines, electrical, compact diesel and mechanical systems through the Equipment and Engine Training Council (EETC). (E-mail interview Oct 30, 2026).

    David Bodzioch has been an ASE Master Technician for 25 years. Dave is also EETC (Equipment and Engine Training Council) certified and taught Recreational Power Equipment at North Montco Technical Career Center. (Electronic communication Oct 29, 2026).

    Lindsay Clancy was being tried for first-degree murder. She admitted to killing her three children and claimed that she suffered from postpartum psychosis. (Photo by CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via the Associated Press).

    Lindsay Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse charged with strangling and killing her three small children in 2023, lost her bid to have her case dismissed Monday, setting the stage for a possible retrial.

    Massachusetts Superior Court Judge William Sullivan’s 17-page ruling found that a retrial would not be considered double jeopardy because Clancy’s initial jury was deadlocked.

    Clancy, 36, was on trial earlier this year for the strangling deaths of her three young children. The case ended in a mistrial after one juror, known as “Juror Doe,” held out for a conviction. Clancy pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, alleging that she was going through postpartum psychosis at the time of the tragedy, according to coverage on Courthouse News Service.

    Sources indicate that last week, a hearing seeking dismissal of the case explored the role of Michael Desronvil, who is referred to as “Juror Doe” in court records. Desronvil was accused of not following the court’s instructions.

    Sullivan found that the evidence “did not reasonably suggest Juror Doe’s inability to deliberate or refusal to follow the law.”.

    On Nov. 2, the prosecution noted it intends to try Clancy again. She initially faced three counts of murder for the deaths of Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months.

    Police sirens can sound very different, from a slow wail to a rapid yelp. Here’s why officers switch tones and what drivers should do.

    Recent findings suggest that everyone recognizes an emergency siren. Or do they?

    According to recent reports, officers can choose different tones to make their vehicles easier to notice on busy streets or open roads. Some departments also use certain sounds for special warnings. With electronic siren systems offering several options, drivers might hear multiple tones during a single emergency response.

    Learn what the common sounds mean, why officers switch between them, whether different tones signal different emergencies, and how drivers should react.

    Different police siren sounds serve different purposes, but they don’t necessarily indicate specific emergencies. Officers often switch tones based on traffic conditions or to get drivers’ attention. A faster siren doesn’t always mean a more serious emergency.

    The most common police siren sounds include:.

    Modern police vehicles typically use electronic sirens that allow officers to switch between these sounds. Older mechanical sirens use a spinning mechanism to produce a traditional wail.

    Industry observers note that officers also adjust their sirens based on traffic conditions. Faster tones can help get drivers’ attention in heavy traffic, while a slower wail may work on quieter roads. Departments set their own policies for siren use, so there isn’t one standard sound for daytime or nighttime driving.

    Industry observers note that regardless of the siren sound, drivers should respond the same way when an emergency vehicle approaches. Drivers should check their mirrors, signal, and safely pull toward the right side of the road to let the police vehicle pass. They should avoid sudden braking or stopping in an intersection.

    Anyone already in an intersection should continue through before pulling over. Drivers waiting at a red light shouldn’t enter the intersection unless an officer directs them to do so. After the police vehicle passes, drivers should check for other emergency vehicles before returning to traffic. Specific rules may vary by state.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that yesterday, the Supreme Court decided to review Mullin v.
    • The Trump administration's position on this problem is badly wrong, and has dangerous implications.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that yesterday, the Supreme Court decided to review Mullin v. RAICES, a case challenging the legality of Donald Trump's January 2025 "invasion" executive order, which bars virtually all legal migration across the southern border. Trump relies on the Guarantee Clause of Article IV, Section 4 of the Constitution, which states that "The United States shall guarantee to every State in this Union a Republican Form of Government, and shall protect each of them against Invasion." The administration claims that illegal migration, drug smuggling, and supposed "public health" risks  qualify as an "invasion" under the Guarantee Clause, thereby authorizing the president to suspend legal migration indefinitely.

    The Trump administration's position on this problem is badly wrong, and has dangerous implications. In my article, "Immigration is Not Invasion" I provide a comprehensive overview of the many reasons why "invasion" - as that term is used in the Constitution and the AEA - must be a military attack, not illegal migration, drug smuggling, or other similar activity. As James Madison put it, "invasion is an operation of war." I provided a shorter overview of the invasion order and its dangerous implications in a 2025 Just Security article.

    Industry observers note that I also go over the dire implications of adopting a broad definition of invasion. Among other things, it would allow the federal government to suspend the writ of habeas corpus (and thereby detain people - including US citizens - without due process) at any time. It would also give state governments the power to "engage in war" against neighboring foreign countries at virtually any time, even without congressional authorization. And there is much more. This case has major implications that go beyond immigration, and threaten the civil liberties of US citizens, as well as recent migrants.

    The Supreme Court could potentially rule against Trump on statutory grounds, without reaching the concern of the definition of "invasion" in the Constitution. That is what the district court and the DC Circuit did. Alternatively, the Court could rule that the president has purely statutory authority to bar these migrants. But if it rejects these statutory arguments, or at least does so in large part, it will have to reach the "invasion" issue. If the justices do reach that issue, it is vital that the reject the administration's position.

    There are also a number of procedural challenges in the case (primarily involving the scope of the remedy), which I will not attempt to go over here.

    This case should not be confused with the related ongoing litigation over the legality of Trump's invocation of the Alien Enemies Act of 1798. The AEA can only be used to detain and deport migrants when there is a declared war, an "invasion," or a "predatory incursion." There, too, the Trump administration claims illegal migration and drug smuggling qualify as an "invasion," and there too it is wrong to do so (on which see  Part III of my article, my amicus brief in the Fifth Circuit AEA case, which I coauthored on behalf of the Brennan Center, the Cato Institute, and others). As detailed in my article, it is highly likely that "invasion" has the same meaning in the AEA and in the four places where that term is used in the Constitution, enacted just a few years earlier.

    Sources indicate that I will likely have more to say about this case in future posts and other writings. Stay tuned!

    #20812. Border Search of Immigration Lawyer's Phone Was Likely Unconstitutional Retaliation for Lawyer's Speech

    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Reason ↗ Open Full Page

    Border Search of Immigration Lawyer's Phone Was Likely Unconstitutional Retaliation for Lawyer's Speech

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Reason

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that from Judge Allison Burroughs (D.
    • Industry observers note that andrew Lattarulo is an immigration lawyer and part owner of the law firm Georges Cote LLP, which represents "thousands of clients in active immigration proceedings." Lattarulo also runs a popular Instagram account featuring videos of himself discussing "know-your-rights information about U.S.
    • According to recent reports, audai Cote, "the registered agent and individual in charge of I-9 compliance" at the firm, was served with a Notice of Inspection on September 8, 2025.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that from Judge Allison Burroughs (D. Mass.) Friday in Lattarulo v. Mullin:.

    Industry observers note that andrew Lattarulo is an immigration lawyer and part owner of the law firm Georges Cote LLP, which represents "thousands of clients in active immigration proceedings." Lattarulo also runs a popular Instagram account featuring videos of himself discussing "know-your-rights information about U.S. immigration matters," which regularly "amasses hundreds of thousands of views." Georges Cote is presently being investigated by Homeland Security Investigations ("HSI"), the investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security ("DHS"), for employing individuals without a legal right to work in the United States.

    According to recent reports, audai Cote, "the registered agent and individual in charge of I-9 compliance" at the firm, was served with a Notice of Inspection on September 8, 2025. Unlike Lattarulo, "Cote is not an immigration attorney—he focuses on personal injury." The firm responded on September 12, 2025, and the government sent Cote a Notice of Suspect Documents on September 25, 2025. The firm was given ten days to attempt to verify the identity and work authorization of the employees named in the Notice of Suspect Documents.

    Recent findings suggest that in late September 2025, while the HSI investigation proceeded, both Lattarulo and Cote travelled from Boston to Aruba for a weekend trip. On September 27, 2025, Cote arrived back at Logan Airport from Aruba without problem. Lattarulo made the same journey the following day, September 28, 2025. Lattarulo passed through customs preclearance in Aruba before boarding a flight to Boston.

    In a recent development, when his flight arrived at Logan Airport, three U.S. Customs and Border Protection ("CBP") agents and one HSI officer stopped Lattarulo as he got off the plane. The agents seized his cell phone without a warrant and then downloaded a complete copy of the data stored on the phone. Eight days later, they returned the cell phone via overnight delivery.

    The seized cell phone data is currently in a format that is not readable or reviewable, but the government intends to convert the data to an accessible format and search it if the Court permits. The data includes confidential information, including privileged attorney-client communications related to Lattarulo's clients. {The Government was clear that any search of the contents of the phone would utilize a taint team to protect privileged information.} ….

    The court held that Lattarulo was likely correct on his claim that the search was unconstitutional retaliation for his speech, and therefore granted "a preliminary injunction enjoining Defendants from accessing the data obtained from the phone before this action is resolved":.

    "[T]he law is settled that as a general matter the First Amendment prohibits government officials from subjecting an individual to retaliatory actions, including criminal prosecutions, for speaking out." … The retaliation issue [here] turns on causation—that is, whether the seizure and search of Lattarulo's cell phone would have occurred but for his protected speech.

    Recent findings suggest that respondents have provided no evidence that searches of cell phones are frequently conducted during the kind of employment investigation at glitch here, and Lattarulo has directed the Court to sources which suggest otherwise. Indeed, Lattarulo's evidence suggests that any pursuit of criminal charges against employers for employing unauthorized immigrants is exceedingly rare. The fact that the government, after Lattarulo spoke out publicly against it, elected to adopt a highly unusual investigative method that appears designed to inflict a maximal burden on Lattarulo lends substantial support to an inference that its actions were pretextual.

    The stage of the investigation at which the search occurred further bolsters the inference of pretext. Under HSI's own policies, the agency "presumes that employers who, within 10 business days of receiving a Notice of Suspect Documents, verify the identity and/or employment authorization of the listed employees, or take appropriate actions to address the apparent employment of unauthorized workers, have demonstrated reasonable care under the INA." The government's search occurred only three days after Georges Cote first received a Notice of Suspect Documents, meaning that the agency was still early in its period of "presum[ing]" compliance when it occurred. Thus, the government's actions here required it to short-circuit its orderly investigative procedures and cast aside its ten-day presumption of compliance in favor of immediately seizing Lattarulo's phone. That aggressive deviation from protocol strongly suggests that the seizure did not arise from an ordinary investigative motive.

    Further, Lattarulo has identified an "otherwise similarly situated individual not engaged in the same sort of protected speech," who was not subjected to the same enforcement action: his law firm partner Audai Cote, who had the same or greater access to the firm's employment records but did not speak publicly about immigrant rights. Indeed, if the government was truly intent on seizing evidence at the first possible opportunity, Mr. Cote, who returned to America a full day before Lattarulo, would have been a more logical target. Nonetheless, the government opted to wait until Lattarulo touched down in Boston the next day and subject only him to an intrusive cell phone search. The balance of the evidence presently before the Court thus suggests that Lattarulo is likely to establish that he would not have been searched except for his protected speech.

    {It is true that the presence of probable cause generally precludes a finding of causation in a retaliatory arrest case, but the Supreme Court has recognized a limited exception for situations in which officers who "have probable cause to make arrests [for a particular crime] … typically exercise their discretion not to do so," such as "an individual who has been vocally complaining about police conduct … [before being] arrested for jaywalking," By analogy, the limited record before the Court suggests that searches of cell phones are not regularly conducted during the kind of employment investigation at problem here and that Lattarulo's own law firm partner was not subjected to the same seizure and search of property.}.

    It is true that Defendants can "prevail … by showing that the [search] would have been initiated without respect to retaliation," and here Defendants state that they have additional evidence which would show as much, but they have not provided it because they assert that doing so would prejudice an ongoing investigation…. [T]he Court concludes that the limited record that is before the Court suggests that Lattarulo is likely to succeed on the merits of his First Amendment retaliation claim and that the record before it is therefore adequate to grant the limited preliminary relief contemplated by this order.

    The court didn't resolve Lattarulo's Fourth Amendment claim, because it granted the preliminary injunction based on the First Amendment claim. But it did note the following:.

    According to recent reports, plaintiffs' Fourth Amendment claim turns largely on the scope of the border search exception to the Fourth Amendment's warrant requirement. That exception "is grounded in the government's 'inherent authority to protect, and a paramount interest in protecting, its territorial integrity.'" It allows the government to perform "routine" border searches of electronic devices without suspicion of any crime, and to perform "non-routine" border searches of electronic devices without a warrant, so long as the government has reasonable suspicion. Alasaad v. Mayorkas (1st Cir. 2021).

    In a recent development, the question this case raises is: reasonable suspicion of what? In other words, what types of suspected criminal activities can the government use a warrantless advanced border search to investigate? The First Circuit in Alasaad stated that the exception applies to searches for "contraband" or for "evidence of contraband or a border-related crime." Later in its opinion, however, it stated that the exception applies to searches for "contraband, evidence of contraband, or for evidence of activity in violation of the laws enforced or administered by CBP or ICE." In most cases, of course, "border-related crime[s]" and "activity in violation of the laws enforced or administered by CBP or ICE" are synonymous, and the First Circuit in Alasaad appears to have intended to use those terms more or less synonymously.

    According to recent reports, the difficulty of this case lies in the fact that the suspected violation at glitch—employment of unauthorized aliens in the United States in violation 8 U.S.C § 1324a—involves a law that is "enforced or administered by CBP or ICE" but arguably is not a "border-related crime." Based on the information before the Court, there appears to be no connection between Lattarulo's border crossing (or, more broadly, the government's interest in policing the border) and the suspected crime that formed the basis for the government's border search. Rather, it appears that the government seized on a fortuitous border crossing following a weekend vacation as an opportunity to search for evidence of a domestic crime it was already investigating.

    Even though the suspected violation involves aliens and a law administered by ICE, the Court is not convinced that the First Circuit in Alasaad intended for the border exception to apply to investigations into activity that occurred nowhere near the border and that has no relationship to the border crossing during which the search occurred. Nor is the Court convinced that application of the border search exception to this type of investigation would further the principles underlying the exception. Nonetheless, given the novelty of these questions and the fact that a ruling on them is not necessary, the Court will refrain at this point from reaching a firm conclusion on the matter of the border search's applicability….

    Mary Lemay and Patrick M. Hanley (Butters Brazilian LLP) represent Lattarulo.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Supreme Court disbarred conservative watchdog group Judicial Watch founder and activist Larry Klayman on Monday following his 18-month suspension issued last year by the District of Columbia Court of Appeals.
    • Supreme Court disbarred conservative watchdog group Judicial Watch founder and activist Larry Klayman on Monday following his 18-month suspension issued last year by the District of Columbia Court of Appeals.
    • Klayman’s disbarment follows a suspension for violating numerous ethical rules in connection to representing rancher Cliven Bundy in Nevada federal court, Law360 reports.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the U.S. Supreme Court disbarred conservative watchdog group Judicial Watch founder and activist Larry Klayman on Monday following his 18-month suspension issued last year by the District of Columbia Court of Appeals. (Image from Shutterstock).

    In a recent development, the U.S. Supreme Court disbarred conservative watchdog group Judicial Watch founder and activist Larry Klayman on Monday following his 18-month suspension issued last year by the District of Columbia Court of Appeals.

    Klayman’s disbarment follows a suspension for violating numerous ethical rules in connection to representing rancher Cliven Bundy in Nevada federal court, Law360 reports.

    According to recent reports, bundy had been facing a criminal case over his 2014 standoff with federal agents when Klayman, a Florida attorney, sought pro hac vice status to join Bundy’s legal team in 2016. The District of Columbia Office of Disciplinary Counsel filed a complaint against Klayman in 2018, claiming that he misled the U.S. District Court for the District of Nevada about his disciplinary status when he tried to represent Bundy. A D.C. appellate court ruling adopted the District of Columbia Bar’s findings and suspension.

    The disciplinary office alleged that Klayman also made baseless claims against the judge who denied his admission to the Nevada court.

    Klayman, in a statement to Law360 on Monday said, “The order contains no factual or legal reasoning, is subject to reconsideration and is not final. I made a compelling submission to the Supreme Court recently, and apparently, it was not considered. This will be a basis for reconsideration.”.

    #20809. Latest Update: Before or After the Snow? Here’s the Right Time to Salt Your Driveway This Winter

    Latest Update: Before or After the Snow? Here’s the Right Time to Salt Your Driveway This Winter

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Familyhandyman

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Salt your driveway like a pro this winter with these expert-backed tips.
    • The Centers for Disease Control report a 35 percent increase in outdoor slips and falls during the winter months.
    • According to recent reports, it depends.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

    Salt your driveway like a pro this winter with these expert-backed tips.

    The Centers for Disease Control report a 35 percent increase in outdoor slips and falls during the winter months. Icy sidewalks, stairs and driveways are largely to blame for this seasonal uptick. Icy driveways are not only dangerous to walk on but also make driving and parking difficult. Ice melt salt is one of the best ways to keep driveways clear, but how should you best use it? Should you apply it before or after a storm — or both? Two industry experts weigh in on the best way to salt your driveway for optimal results this winter.

    According to recent reports, it depends. Salting before a big storm with heavy snow and ice accumulation is a good idea, but timing matters.

    According to recent reports, initiative to apply salt several hours before a storm hits for best results. It creates a salty coating that prevents the initial snowfall from bonding with the driveway surface. Pre-salting reduces total snow accumulation and makes snow removal easier once the storm is over. Avoid doing it too far in advance, or if rain is in the forecast, as the salt can be washed or blown away before the snow arrives. It’s not necessary to salt before a light snowfall of less than six inches.

    It’s always a good idea to salt after it snows, but don’t rely on it to replace snow removal efforts. First remove as much snow as possible with a shovel or snowblower, then use salt to clear away any remaining slush and snow.

    Sources indicate that the best time to salt is immediately after snow removal, before cold nighttime temperatures set in. “When applied before the temperatures drop, salt prevents ice from forming and ensures the snow does not freeze solid to the ground,” Angelika Klimorowski, a winter maintenance specialist at Online Rock Salt, notes.

    Apply salt before and after a significant storm for best results, especially when heavy snow, sleet or freezing rain is expected.

    “Pre-salting helps prevent ice from bonding to the driveway, while a second application can help break down any ice that forms,” Aaron Strickland, owner of Mr. Trim Lawn & Garden Services, claims. “For a typical snowfall, both applications usually aren’t necessary.”.

    According to recent reports, if only a few inches of snow is forecast, salting after snow removal is likely sufficient. Applying salt before and after a small storm is not only a waste of money, but can damage driveway surfaces, burn lawn edges and generate harmful storm runoff.

    “The exact amount of rock salt that you need will depend on how big the area is that you are planning to de-ice,” Klimorowski indicates. A little goes a long way, and more is not better. A 12-oz. coffee mug filled with salt is enough to treat a 1,000-sq.-ft. driveway. Spread salt evenly, leaving about 3 inches between salt grains. Avoid overapplication, as it can degrade driveway surfaces and harm the environment.

    It has been revealed that A handheld spreader makes application easier and more consistent, especially for larger driveways. “We try to follow recommended coverage rates and use a spreader wherever possible,” Strickland indicates. “Too much salt wastes product and can damage surrounding grass and gardens.” If spreading salt by hand, always wear gloves and cascade it for even coverage.

    In a recent development, rock salt is only effective down to ground temperatures of 15 to 17 degrees. Don’t apply more salt if it’s not working, as it’s likely too cold out for it to work. “If your area tends to experience colder temperatures, you may need to find an alternative de-icing product to keep your surfaces safe,” Klimorowski claims. Calcium chloride and magnesium chloride ice melt products are two common alternatives that remain effective at sub-zero temperatures.

    Yes, rain will wash away salt rather than dissolve it. It then ends up in storm drains and potentially pollutes local bodies of water.

    Rock salt stops working in temperatures below 10 to 15 degrees.

    “While it is true that salt will work best if you apply it before the temperatures drop, there is no deadline, and you can always apply it later,” Klimorowski says.

    It has been revealed that there’s no guarantee salt will damage your driveway, but you should use it sparingly. Concrete driveways are particularly vulnerable to salt damage.

    How to Shovel the Trickiest Surfaces the Right Way, From Pavers to Your Roof

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1176 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Familyhandyman

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • From lawns to sealed concrete, you might be surprised at how much damage a snow shovel can do.
    • Sources indicate that clearing snow from walkways is vital for safety, but winter shoveling can easily damage wooden decks, asphalt driveways and other surfaces.
    • It has been revealed that “Snow can camouflage uneven areas and patches of ice, posing slip-and-fall risks, particularly when you’re rushing to shovel,” indicates landscaping expert Jose Lopez.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

    From lawns to sealed concrete, you might be surprised at how much damage a snow shovel can do.

    Sources indicate that clearing snow from walkways is vital for safety, but winter shoveling can easily damage wooden decks, asphalt driveways and other surfaces. So, as the days get shorter and colder, it’s important to solidify your shoveling proposal before the first snow flies.

    It has been revealed that “Snow can camouflage uneven areas and patches of ice, posing slip-and-fall risks, particularly when you’re rushing to shovel,” indicates landscaping expert Jose Lopez. “Being mindful and taking a relaxed, careful approach will help you save money and keep everyone safe all winter long.”.

    Ahead, experts walk through how to shovel eleven tricky surfaces around your home, to keep everyone safe, plus prevent costly springtime repairs.

    It has been revealed that shoveling gravel is frustrating because those pebbles tend to come up with the snow, then get scattered onto the landscaping. “You will end up cleaning about $150 worth of it off your lawn in the spring,” claims grading and paving contractor Scott Flores.

    To make life easier, use a plastic shovel, keep the blade about an inch above the gravel and clear the snow in short passes. “You don’t have to expose all of the gravel,” notes Lopez. “It’s fine to leave a thin layer of snow behind.”.

    Recent findings suggest that A metal snow shovel blade can actually scratch and gouge concrete. “It can cause $3,000 worth of damage to your pavement in 20 minutes and you won’t know it ’til April,” states Flores. Initially, the damage “may not look like much, but once water gets under it and freezes, it will cause spalling and make your pavement look 10 years older than it is.”.

    Luckily, the fix is easy on this one: always use a poly-blade (plastic) or rubber-edged shovel on concrete.

    Aliaksandr Bahdanovich/Getty Images.

    Aggressive shoveling can damage paint and sealers, even if they’re touted as “scratch-resistant.” “That layer is about three millimeters thick, and your steel shovel will chip it away like you’re peeling your fingernails,” says Flores.

    The fix: use a poly-blade shovel, shovel with a slight upward motion and leave a half-inch of snow for the sun to melt, says Flores. “Many believe that steel shovels will last longer. Yes they will, but that’s what makes them bad,” he says.

    Pro-tip: If you use a deicer, make sure it’s safe for your particular coating, claims Lopez.

    In a recent development, just like with concrete, asphalt seems indestructible, but metal shovels can damage it, especially if it already has imperfections or cracks. So, the best approach is to use a poly-blade (plastic) or rubber-edged shovel, and shovel the snow before it partially melts and refreezes.

    “Avoid pushing your shovel into cracks or potholes, and don’t bang it against the surface in an attempt to dislodge stubborn ice,” indicates Lopez. “Instead, choose a deicing product that’s safe for asphalt.”.

    It has been revealed that A shovel can easily catch the edge of a paver and scratch, break or knock it out of place. To prevent that, use a poly-blade shovel, take shorter shovel strokes, push snow at an angle and slightly raise up the leading edge.

    “Shoveling and deicing aggressively won’t make your job faster or easier, it takes some finesse,” says Lopez. Also, use de-icers that are safe for both the paving and jointing material, and inspect the walkway for loose bricks once the snow melts.

    After a snow, it can be tricky to tell where the concrete ends and the lawn begins, and one wrong move means damaged grass come springtime. To keep from marring your grass, mark walkway edges with small flags before it snows. While shoveling, keep the blade even with your walkway, versus angling it toward the grass.

    Pro-tip: “Slow down and work in short passes near the edges, rather than trying to force the shovel along,” says Lopez. “.

    Try not to pile snow on shrubs and other perennials, as that can snap branches. It’s also best to keep deicers and their runoff away from landscaping.

    Sources indicate that “Before winter arrives, proposal where you’ll pile or toss snow to keep it away from sensitive plants,” claims Lopez. “You may find it helpful to use a smaller shovel, which will give you better control over where the snow lands.”.

    Also, try not to move soil, which can expose plants to the cold, and never strike frozen branches to remove snow. “Wood breaks more easily than people expect,” claims moving professional Leon Schwab.

    Recent findings suggest that aggressive shoveling is sure to damage a deck, regardless of its composition. To preserve yours, use a poly-blade shovel and push the snow in the direction of the boards. If it’s safe to do so, leave a thin layer of snow, instead of shoveling all the way down to bare decking, then apply a deicer that’s recommended for the surface type.

    Safety tip: “If wet, heavy snow is accumulating and you notice the deck sagging or hear creaking noises, seek professional advice,” says Lopez. “Don’t continue using the deck if you suspect a structural problem.”.

    Stairs are particularly hazardous when its slippery out, and clearing them can be precarious, with snow obscuring their boundaries and confined spaces limiting your range of motion.

    According to recent reports, to stay safe, “Wear boots with good traction and make sure your staircase is well lit,” notes Lopez. “Don’t rush the job. It’s better to take your time and shovel safely.”.

    Pro-tip: “Use a small shovel to clear one step at a time and maintain a stable position,” says Schwab.

    According to recent reports, sometimes it’s prudent to clear large accumulations of snow from the roof, but it’s also a dangerous job. To stay safe, roofing contractor Andre Kazimierski recommends using a roof rake, which allows you to pull off snow while remaining on the ground. Focus on clearing off as much as you can, but don’t worry about leaving it completely bare, and try not to touch your roofing material.

    It has been revealed that “Do this sooner rather than later, because if it starts to warm up a bit the snow will become denser and heavier, making it harder to remove,” notes Kazimierski. “And never walk on your roof when it’s even the slightest bit snowy or icy up there.”.

    Obviously, you don’t want to take a shovel to your car, as that would do a lot of damage. Instead, use a snow brush or broom that’s designed to be gentle on vehicle finishes. Flores recommends this one from Snow Joe.

    Start by clearing the roof in sections, then move on to the hood, trunk, windows, headlights, taillights and mirrors. You’ll especially want to get the roof and hood fully clear; otherwise, once you start driving, snow can blow up or slide down onto your windshield, obstructing your vision and endangering other drivers. “That ice can fly off your car at 40 miles per hour,” claims Flores.

    A Los Angeles County Superior Court judge has been removed from his position for making inappropriate racial and sexual comments and several other instances of misconduct.

    In its decision Tuesday, the California Commission on Judicial Performance noted Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Robert Draper “persistently violated the standards governing judicial behavior and engaged in extensive and severe misconduct.” The commission also said the judge failed to accept responsibility or show remorse for his actions.

    Courthouse News Service has the story.

    Among the charges, the commission considered Draper’s conduct during a February 2023 posttrial hearing in a sexual harassment case, where he lectured a Black attorney about Black football players and race relations in the South. It also examined comments that Draper made to female attorneys in the case—while in his chambers—about male attorneys who slept with their secretaries at his prior law firm.

    Other charges alleged that Draper made inappropriate comments to a female colleague and a female court personnel, engaged in improper ex parte communications, and improperly disclosed confidential juvenile records.

    Draper has noted the charges “were contrary to all credible evidence and/or taken wholly out of context.”.

    An attorney who represented Draper didn’t respond to a request for comment from Courthouse News Service.

    Judge denies allegations he made inappropriate comments during disciplinary hearing.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The 2026 Federalist Society Convention is a wrap.
    • I think much of the press coverage failed in attempt to to consolidate a very broad movement into a few paragraphs.
    • It has been revealed that I think there are a range of opinions about how the conservative legal movement should respond to the current political situation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The 2026 Federalist Society Convention is a wrap. I have attended every NLC since I was a 1L in 2006 (except for the cancelled COVID year). At each convention, the focus is a bit different but the overall takeaway is similar. There is a healthy a mix of timeless topics and topical topics, with an infusion of the political landscape of the day. It is very hard to capture the essence of a convention by watching some or even all of the panels, as so much business transpires in the hallways and at the bars.

    I think much of the press coverage failed in attempt to to consolidate a very broad movement into a few paragraphs. For example, CNN blared "After blue wave, Federalist Society is ready to move on from Trump." Really? Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered the Olson Lecture, White House Counsel Will Scharf had a fireside chat, White House Advisor May Mailman discussed over-regulation, and Gene Hamilton favored restrictive immigration policy on behalf of America First Legal Foundation. Plus there were other members of the administration from the EPA and OLP.

    It has been revealed that I think there are a range of opinions about how the conservative legal movement should respond to the current political situation. I don't think anyone actually knows exactly what to do. The midterm election, of course, was the elephant in the room. I offered my take here. A lot can happen over the next two years.

    It has been revealed that I'm flummoxed by the uproar about the commemorative coins celebrating Calais, Slaughter, and other decision. These were in fact generational wins at the Supreme Court. Justice Scalia established overruling Humphrey's Executor as a founding principle of FedSoc. Since the 1980s, conservatives--including John Roberts--have seen the Voting Rights Act as violating the Constitution. And West Virginia v. B.P.J. was such an obvious outcome--except perhaps at CNN. Plus, this was the swaggiest NLC I've ever been to. There was an entire room to pick up FedSoc swag. The coins were a nice touch.

    According to recent reports, perhaps the biggest disruption at the convention was the groundstop. My flight home Saturday evening was cancelled, as were many others. I was able to get a room at the Mayflower for another day. Fortunately, one of the few remaining perks of United status is priority rebooking during "irregular operations." I was originally scheduled to fly home Sunday evening around 7:30 p.m. The United App has a fresh feature that lets you be on standby for up to three flights at once without losing your confirmed seat. United will send you a text notifying you that a seat opened up on an earlier flight, and you have twenty minutes to accept it. I was able to jump from the 7:30 p.m. flight to the 12:50 p.m. flight. A few hours later, I was given a chance to jump from the 12:50 p.m. flight to the 10:58 a.m. flight. For both of these flights, I was number one on the standby list. Around 5:00 a.m., I was offered the chance to move to the 8:20 a.m. flight, but I was sleeping and missed the window. The system worked very well. And without my status, I doubt I would have been able to get the earlier flight. As things turned out, the 12:50 p.m. flight was cancelled. I will get home today.

    • In a recent development, last year, Texas enacted one of the country's most expansive school-choice policies.
    • Last year, Texas enacted one of the country's most expansive school-choice policies.
    • Recent findings suggest that school choice at this scale is worth celebrating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, last year, Texas enacted one of the country's most expansive school-choice policies. The Texas Education Freedom Accounts program now serves more than 100,000 students, enabling families to choose the learning environments that align with their values and best meet their children’s learning needs.School choice at this scale is worth celebrating. School-choice policies reflect the Constitution’s commitment to religious liberty and America’s longstanding recognition that parents, not the state, are the primary educators of their children.A century ago, the Supreme Court struck down a Ku Klux Klan-backed Oregon law that would have banned private schooling, ruling in Pierce v. Society of Sisters that “the child is not the mere creature of the state.” Parents, the Court recognized, have the right and primary authority “to direct the upbringing and education” of their children.Half a century later, in Yoder v. Wisconsin, the Court reaffirmed the “fundamental interest of parents to guide the religious future and education of their children.” The Court declared that only “interests of the highest order” can override these fundamental freedoms.The Espinoza v. Montana Department of Revenue (2020) and Carson v. Makin (2022) decisions built on that foundation, holding that states cannot exclude otherwise qualified private schools from generally available scholarship programs merely because they are religious. The Court ruled that such discrimination is “odious to the Constitution.”But Texas policymakers are now facing a question that school-choice advocates cannot avoid: What if parents choose schools funded by foreign adversaries that indoctrinate students to hate people who are not like them, and whose founders and staff have documented ties to terrorist organizations?>>> School Choice Is About Religious Liberty, Not Just Better Test ScoresWhat is the limit of school choice?Earlier this year, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott drew a line when he declared: “There’s no school choice for schools with ties to organizations that have connections to terrorism.” Several months earlier, Abbott had designated the Muslim Brotherhood and the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) as foreign terrorist organizations. (CAIR is challenging that designation.)After those designations, acting comptroller Kelly Hancock wrote to Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton asking whether schools with ties to those organizations or the Chinese government could be excluded from the TEFA program. Paxton’s reply was unambiguous: “Let me be crystal clear: Texans’ tax dollars should never fund Islamic terrorists or America’s enemies.” Hancock then announced no schools with such ties would receive Texas tax dollars through TEFA.That principle—that public funds should not flow to schools with ties to terrorist organizations or hostile foreign powers—is sound. All freedoms have limits. Liberty is not license. A state has a compelling interest in ensuring that taxpayer dollars do not subsidize the indoctrination of children to hate America or to support terrorism.But even the soundest principle can be implemented in an unsound, or even unconstitutional manner.In March 2026, Houston-area attorney and father Mehdi Cherkaoui filed a federal lawsuit against Paxton, Hancock, and Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath, alleging that state officials had “systematically targeted Islamic schools for exclusion based on their religious identity.” His complaint observed that as of early 2026, hundreds of private schools across Texas—including numerous Christian schools—had been approved for TEFA, while not a single accredited Islamic school had been admitted. Cherkaoui sought to use TEFA funds to cover his children’s tuition at the Houston Quran Academy, but the school was not approved under the program. Three Islamic schools and additional parents joined a second suit shortly thereafter.State officials denied the discrimination charge, explaining to the court that the comptroller’s office “had complications with processing and reviewing schools accredited by the nonprofit Cognia, regardless of whether they have Islamic affiliations.”U.S. District Judge Alfred H. Bennett was not satisfied with that explanation. On March 17, hours before the original application deadline, he issued a temporary restraining order. At the emergency hearing, Bennett called the complete absence of approved Islamic schools “troubling,” remarking: “If you were to roll dice in a game of chance… you would not come up with those numbers. The appearance of this reeks.” He extended the student application deadline to March 31 and ordered state officials to receive and process applications from Islamic schools through the normal TEFA process. Within days, four Islamic schools were admitted: Brighter Horizons Academy in Garland, Bayaan Academy, Excellence Academy near Plano, and the Houston Quran Academy.If it is true that the Muslim schools were not approved solely due to their religious affiliation, that would be a clear violation of their First Amendment rights. The Constitution’s guarantee of religious liberty undoubtedly prohibits such blanket discrimination.However, the story is not so clear-cut. Makin (2022) decisions built on that foundation, holding that states cannot exclude otherwise qualified private schools from generally available scholarship programs merely because they are religious.     💡 Key Takeaways
